value.body: Food product developers design new foods and beverages or change existing ones, for taste, cost, nutrition or shelf life. Food and beverage companies, ingredient suppliers and contract manufacturers hire them. The work moves between a pilot kitchen or lab, tasting panels and factory trials.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Food Technology or B.Sc Food Science

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Pilot plant equipment, sensory evaluation, nutrition labelling data

items.label: Jobs in registered food-processing units
items.note: About 12.4% of employment in registered factories; R&D roles are a small part
items.source: Annual Survey of Industries 2022-23, via MoFPI Lok Sabha reply, Feb 2025 (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as R&D or new product development trainees, sometimes after starting in quality control. Internships in a food plant or R&D lab, and a grasp of FSSAI standards and labelling rules, help.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many trials do not reach the market; iteration is normal.
Next steps: senior developer, R&D manager, or regulatory roles.
A master's degree helps for research-heavy positions.
